name: Foresight Institute AI for Science & Safety Grants (Nodes RFP)
amount: Typically USD 30,000-100,000 (larger possible); overhead up to 10%
eligibility: Individuals, teams, non-profits and for-profits; AI safety, local compute, coordination/accountability, AI-first science; outputs must be open-sourced
eligibility_note: RFP page lists no nationality/citizenship restriction; priority to applicants who will be in-person in SF or Berlin hubs; due diligence required.
how_to_apply_tip: Current round closes 31 Oct 2026 (23:59 PDT); if missed, watch foresight.org/grants for the next RFP. Remote applicants should explain how they will engage with the hubs.
deadline_quote: The application deadline for this RFP is 31st October 2026 23:59 PDT.
verdict_reason: Individuals, teams and organizations may apply, and the page sets no nationality, institution, age or career-stage restriction. The deadline is today (2026-10-31, 23:59 PDT), so only hours remain. In-person hub presence is prioritised but not required.
eligibility_quote: Who can apply? We accept applications from individuals, teams, and organizations. Both non-profit and for-profit organizations are welcome to apply, but for-profits should be prepared to motivate why they need grant funding. ... Successful applicants must pass our due diligence process.

name: NLnet Foundation Open Calls (NGI Zero / Restack / CodeSupply funds)
amount: EUR 5,000-50,000 for a first grant
eligibility: Individuals or organisations doing open-source technical development (open licences required)
eligibility_note: Any country can apply, but EU-funded calls usually expect Horizon Europe-eligible applicants; others must justify a 'European dimension'.
how_to_apply_tip: Bimonthly deadlines; partner with a European collaborator or show EU user benefit. Proposal must be human-written (AI use disclosed).
deadline_quote: Next deadline: November 3rd 2026 12:00 CET (noon)
verdict_reason: Pakistan is on NLnet's list of Horizon Europe-eligible countries, so the European-dimension requirement is met. Its applicants participate on the same terms as EU applicants. Grants are for open-source technical development rather than pure research.
eligibility_quote: Our EU-supported funds require a strong European dimension; usually this means applicants should (mostly) be from Horizon Europe-eligible countries. / People and organisations of these eligible countries can participate on the same terms as those from EU member states. (European-dimension page country list includes 'Pakistan')

name: Emergent Ventures
amount: See website (fellowships/grants, typically small)
eligibility: Anyone 13+ worldwide with high-impact 'zero to one' ideas; no credentials required
eligibility_note: Supports 'thinkers and doers worldwide'; no country restriction stated (dedicated tranches for India, Africa, etc.).
how_to_apply_tip: Short, punchy application; AI-written applications are explicitly not accepted. Pitch an ambitious AI project with societal impact.
deadline_quote: There is no application deadline for EV AI, but applicants are encouraged to apply quickly, as funds are limited. (Main EV page shows an 'Apply Now' form and no deadline.)
verdict_reason: The programme supports people worldwide and its only stated condition is a minimum age of 13. Nothing excludes a Pakistani academic. AI-written applications are rejected.
eligibility_quote: supporting thinkers and doers worldwide who pursue highly scalable, "zero to one" ideas to meaningfully improve society ... Applicants must be at least 13 years old.

name: Internet Freedom Fund (incl. applied research)
eligibility: Individuals 18+ and organisations; technology or applied research projects helping people facing censorship/surveillance
eligibility_note: Open 'regardless of nationality'; only OFAC-sanctioned countries excluded (Pakistan is not).
how_to_apply_tip: Submit a concept note first (response in ~6-8 weeks); ML-based censorship measurement or deepfake/surveillance detection fits.
deadline_quote: Applications to the Fund go through a two-stage application process and are accepted on a rolling basis.
verdict_reason: Individuals aged 18 or over may apply regardless of nationality, and only US-sanctioned countries are excluded. Pakistan is not under OFAC country-wide sanctions. The project must fit internet freedom (censorship or surveillance).
eligibility_quote: Individuals ages 18+ or organizations (for-profit or nonprofit) irrespective of nationality, creed, or sex are eligible to apply. OTF is not able to support applicants within countries that the United States has trade restrictions or export sanctions as determined by the U.S. Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC).

name: Transformative AI Fund (successor to Long-Term Future Fund)
amount: Typically USD 10,000-150,000; rarely above USD 300,000
eligibility: Individuals, new and existing organisations; technical AI safety research, policy, forecasting, field-building, training
eligibility_note: Official page states no country restriction and funds individuals; Long-Term Future Fund is closed and replaced by this fund.
how_to_apply_tip: Short online form (<1h). Frame a concrete 6-12 month AI safety project (e.g. interpretability/evals) with a modest budget; small, well-scoped asks from early-career researchers are common.
deadline_quote: We are always open to applications.
verdict_reason: The fund grants to individuals and states no geographic, age or institutional restriction. An AI safety or AI-risk project from a Pakistan-based researcher is within remit.
eligibility_quote: We make early-stage grants to individuals, new organizations, and existing organizations with new projects, addressing transformative AI, with a primary focus on reducing global catastrophic risks from advanced AI systems.

name: Cooperative AI Foundation Research Grants (incl. Early-Career Track)
amount: Min GBP 10,000; early-career track max GBP 100,000 (up to 12 months); past grants GBP 10k-385k (median ~GBP 150k); overhead max 10% of direct costs
duration: Up to 12 months (early-career track); up to 2 years (standard)
eligibility: Researchers anywhere; early-career track for postdocs/junior researchers typically within 2-3 years of PhD; projects in cooperative AI research areas
eligibility_note: Grants page: 'applicants can be located anywhere in the world'; affiliation helpful but not required.
how_to_apply_tip: Early-career track fits a 0-3 yr postdoc exactly; read their research-area list and sign up to the newsletter, since rounds open with a pre-proposal stage.
deadline_quote: Our first grant deadline for 2025 has passed and we are no longer accepting applications. ... To stay informed about future opportunities, please sign up for our newsletter below or revisit this page for updates.
verdict_reason: Official page sets no nationality, institution, age or gender restriction; affiliation not required; early-career track expects applicants within 2-3 years of PhD, which a <2-year PhD meets. No round is currently open, so this applies to the next call's terms if unchanged.
eligibility_quote: You can be located anywhere in the world. ... An affiliation can, in many cases, strengthen your proposal, but is not required. ... We expect most early-career applicants to apply within 2-3 years of completing their PhD.

name: ISIF Asia Grants
eligibility: Organisations (government, private, NGO incl. universities) registered in APNIC service region; Internet-for-development projects
eligibility_note: Lead organisation must be registered in one of 56 APNIC economies; Pakistan is in the service region. Individuals cannot apply.
how_to_apply_tip: Apply through your university/ORIC as the lead organisation; frame an AI-enabled connectivity or community-network project.
deadline_quote: The call for concept notes for ISIF Asia 2026 has now closed. ... The next round of concept notes will be open in 2027.
verdict_reason: Any organisation type (incl. private companies) registered in an APNIC economy may lead; Pakistan is in the APNIC Foundation service region. Must apply through BIC as lead organisation, not as an individual.
eligibility_quote: Individuals are not eligible to apply. ... Any kind of organisation can apply, including government departments, private companies, and non-government organisations ... led by an organisation registered in one of the 56 economies in the APNIC Foundation service region. (Service region page, South Asia: Pakistan, PK.)

name: Wikimedia Research Fund
amount: Type 1: USD 2,000-50,000 (12 months); Type 2: up to USD 150,000 (max 75k/yr, 24 months); Type 3: up to USD 50,000
duration: Up to 12 months (Type 1/3); up to 24 months (Type 2)
eligibility: Individuals, groups, organisations; established researchers in Wikimedia research or wishing to enter it (NLP, ML, knowledge graphs fit well)
eligibility_note: No country restriction; welcomes 'all regions of the world' and particularly encourages Asia, Africa, Latin America, Eastern Europe.
how_to_apply_tip: Strong fit for Urdu/regional-language NLP on Wikipedia/Wikidata; use the program's 1:1 office hours before the January LOI.
deadline_quote: Submissions for Type I and II Research Proposals are now closed. (2025-26 cycle: Letter of Intent January 16, 2026; full proposals April 3, 2026; all deadlines 23:59 Anywhere on Earth.)
verdict_reason: Individuals may apply; no country, institution, age or gender restriction on the official page, and Asia is explicitly encouraged. Next cycle not yet announced.
eligibility_quote: Individuals, groups, and organizations may apply ... established Wikimedia researchers, or established researchers who want to become Wikimedia researchers ... particularly encourages researchers in Central and South America, Africa, Eastern Europe, and Asia.

name: Ethereum Foundation Ecosystem Support Program (Wishlist & RFP grants)
amount: Based on scope (RFPs may give budget guidance); paid in ETH
eligibility: Open-source, non-commercial projects (incl. research) improving Ethereum, aligned with censorship resistance, open source, privacy, security; individuals, academics and teams.
eligibility_note: Official applicants page mentions no country restrictions.
how_to_apply_tip: Respond to a specific Wishlist/RFP item (e.g. cryptography, ZK, security/ML tooling); reviews take 3–6 weeks.
deadline_quote: There are currently no active wishlists available for application. ... There are currently no active Request for Proposals available for application. ... There are no active grant rounds at this time.
verdict_reason: Official applicants page states no country, institution, age or gender restriction (even for-profits may apply for open-source work); however, nothing is currently open to apply to.
eligibility_quote: ESP supports eligible projects working to improve Ethereum ... For-profit companies are welcome to apply if the grant-funded work is open-source. (No country restrictions stated.)

name: Anthropic AI for Science Program (API credits)
amount: Up to USD 20,000 in API credits for a 6-month period
eligibility: Researchers at academic or non-profit research institutions working on high-impact scientific topics; Computer Science explicitly listed (biology/life sciences is a particular focus).
eligibility_note: No nationality restriction on the program page; Anthropic's supported-countries list includes Pakistan.
how_to_apply_tip: Frame the work as AI-for-science (e.g. AI applied to health, climate or materials) rather than pure ML; group collaborators under one organisation ID application. Unsuccessful applicants get no reply.
deadline_quote: We evaluate submissions on the first Monday of each month.
verdict_reason: Program targets researchers in academia with no nationality, age, gender or career-stage limit; as faculty at an academic institution in Pakistan (an Anthropic-supported country) the profile is covered.
eligibility_quote: The program serves "researchers in academia and nonprofit organizations working on scientific research topics we consider high priority"; FAQ: "researchers attached to research institutions." Supported-countries page: products and services are "available only in the countries and regions listed below" (list includes Pakistan).

name: Cohere Labs Catalyst Grants
amount: Cohere API credits (amount not published; more can be requested)
eligibility: Academic partners and civic/public-impact organisations doing public-benefit or open-science research (focus: education, healthcare, climate, sustainability).
eligibility_note: Official page lists no geographic limits and highlights grantees from many countries.
how_to_apply_tip: Strong fit for multilingual/Urdu NLP or low-resource language projects; emphasise open-science outputs and public benefit.
deadline_quote: Applications are considered on a rolling basis.
verdict_reason: Open to academic partners for public-benefit/open-science research; no geographic, age, gender or career-stage restriction on the official page.
eligibility_quote: The grants "enable academic partners, civic and public impact organizations to access Cohere's models through the Cohere API." "Projects must be for public benefit or open science research."

name: Gemini Academic Program (Gemini API credits for research)
amount: Gemini API credits and higher rate limits (amount at Google's discretion)
eligibility: Qualified academic researchers (faculty, staff, PhD students) affiliated with an academic institution or research organisation; priority areas: evaluations/benchmarks, scientific discovery, embodied AI/robotics, emergent capabilities, multimodal understanding.
eligibility_note: Open to researchers in Gemini API supported countries; Google's available-regions page lists Pakistan.
how_to_apply_tip: Frame the project as an evaluation/benchmark or multimodal study and give a concrete token-usage estimate; postdocs should apply as institutional research staff.
deadline_quote: We review applications on a monthly basis.
verdict_reason: Faculty affiliated with an academic institution in a Gemini-supported country qualify; Pakistan is on the available-regions list and AI/robotics (embodied AI) is a priority area.
eligibility_quote: "Qualified academic researchers (such as faculty, staff, and PhD students)" ... "Only individuals (faculty members, researchers or equivalent) affiliated with a valid academic institution" can apply. Available regions: "The Gemini API and Google AI Studio are available in the following countries and territories" (includes Pakistan).

name: Hugging Face Community GPU Grants (Spaces)
amount: Free GPU hardware upgrade for a Hugging Face Space (e.g. T4/A10G/A100 class)
eligibility: Anyone with an innovative, public Hugging Face Space/demo.
eligibility_note: Official docs set no nationality or institutional requirement.
how_to_apply_tip: Request from your Space's Settings (hardware / sleep-time section). Note the docs say creating a new Space that runs on compute (Gradio or Docker) requires a paid plan; static Spaces are free.
deadline_quote: We love helping out those with an innovative Space so please feel free to apply for a community GPU grant and see if yours makes the cut!
verdict_reason: Official docs set no nationality, institution, age or career-stage condition; any owner of an innovative Space can apply.
eligibility_quote: "Do you have an awesome Space but need help covering the GPU hardware upgrade costs? We love helping out those with an innovative Space so please feel free to apply for a community GPU grant" ... "This application can be found in your Space hardware repo settings."

name: TPU Research Cloud (TRC)
amount: Free access to Cloud TPUs (cluster of 1,000+ TPU devices); other GCP costs (VMs, storage) not covered
eligibility: Researchers worldwide; must share TRC-supported research publicly (papers/open source) and give feedback to Google.
eligibility_note: Official FAQ: 'Anyone can express interest'; no country restrictions stated (Google Cloud account required, which is available in Pakistan).
how_to_apply_tip: Fill the short 'Express interest' form; have JAX/PyTorch-XLA code ready because the free quota clock starts once invited – pair with Google Cloud Research Credits to cover VM/storage costs.
deadline_quote: Invitations are sent out to approved applicants on a rolling basis.
verdict_reason: Official FAQ says anyone can express interest; no nationality, institution, age or career-stage restriction.
eligibility_quote: "Anyone can express interest in joining the program by signing up at sites.research.google/trc." "Researchers accepted into the TRC program will have access to Cloud TPUs at no charge."

name: Weights & Biases Academic (free research license)
amount: Free W&B platform access for academic research (in-kind)
eligibility: Students, educators and academic researchers.
eligibility_note: Official page: 'Free for students, educators, and academic researchers. Always.' – no country restriction mentioned.
how_to_apply_tip: Sign up with your university email to get the academic tier; useful as in-kind support to list in grant budgets.
deadline_quote: Free for students, educators, and academic researchers. Always.
verdict_reason: Free access is offered to educators and academic researchers with no country or institution restriction stated; the profile is an educator/academic researcher.
eligibility_quote: "Free for students, educators, and academic researchers. Always."

name: SIGCHI Gary Marsden Travel Awards
amount: Depends on funds available and applications per cycle (complimentary registration codes + reimbursement of flights, lodging, meals, local transport, childcare; visa fees excluded)
duration: One-off per conference (physical travel support max once every 3 years)
eligibility: Students, early-career researchers (up to 5 years post-graduation), or those facing financial hardship / lacking institutional support; must be SIGCHI member when applying; attending SIGCHI-sponsored/in-cooperation conferences
eligibility_note: No nationality restriction stated; priority to financial need and benefit to applicant, which favours researchers from low-income countries.
how_to_apply_tip: Next deadlines 2026-11-09 then 2027-01-09 (11:59 PM AoE); conference must start more than one month after the deadline. Good fit: HRI (ACM/IEEE Human-Robot Interaction) is SIGCHI-sponsored. Buy SIGCHI (not just ACM) membership before submitting on Submittable.
deadline_quote: There are seven deadlines: the 9th of January, February, March, May, July, September, and November at 11:59 PM AoE
verdict_reason: PhD within 5 years meets the early-career rule and no nationality restriction exists; conditional on holding SIGCHI membership at application and attending a SIGCHI-sponsored/in-cooperation conference starting more than one month after the chosen deadline.
eligibility_quote: Targets "early-career researchers (such as those who are ≤ 5 years post-graduation)" and those "experiencing financial hardship or lacking institutional support." "You must be a SIGCHI member at the time of application to be eligible." "For physical travel, you can only receive support once every three years."

name: SIGPLAN PAC Travel Grants (incl. Long-Distance International Travel)
amount: Not fixed for long-distance grant; covers travel costs (airfare, lodging, registration); meals capped at USD 50/day in US, USD 60/day outside US
eligibility: SIGPLAN members presenting or serving on committees at SIGPLAN-sponsored events; long-distance grant for members living in Asia, Africa, Australia or South America; separate support for historically marginalized groups (no membership needed)
eligibility_note: Long-Distance International Travel grant explicitly targets members residing in Asia, Africa, Australia or South America - Pakistan (Asia) qualifies.
how_to_apply_tip: Submit at least 4 weeks before the conference's early-registration and early-hotel deadlines; funds are first-come first-served. Relevant if you publish ML-for-code / PL+AI work at PLDI, POPL, OOPSLA etc.
deadline_quote: "Travel requests for conferences are due at least four weeks before the early registration deadline and the early hotel reservation deadline of the conference."
verdict_reason: Long-Distance International Travel grant positively covers SIGPLAN members residing in Asia (Pakistan); no age, career-stage or institution restriction stated. Requires SIGPLAN membership and a SIGPLAN-sponsored event.
eligibility_quote: Long-distance international travel: "Applicants must be SIGPLAN members residing in Asia, Africa, Australia, or South America." Professional members: "Applicants must be SIGPLAN members and provide their ACM membership number."

name: ACL-family Diversity & Inclusion Subsidies (ACL, EMNLP, NAACL, EACL, AACL)
amount: Varies: travel + accommodation reimbursement, registration waiver, caregiving, bandwidth/VPN, ACL membership
eligibility: Students and researchers from underrepresented communities facing financial barriers; priority to authors and first-time attendees
eligibility_note: No country list; official call cites applicants from developing countries as an example; AACL-IJCNLP form explicitly targets 'researchers from developing countries'.
how_to_apply_tip: Reimbursement is post-conference with receipts, so book refundable tickets in case of visa denial.
deadline_quote: ACL 2026: applications due "May 15, 2026" (AoE); no 2027 ACL/EACL/NAACL D&I call found.
verdict_reason: Open to researchers facing financial barriers with no country, age or career-stage restriction; living in a developing country is given as a valid justification.
eligibility_quote: Encourages applications from "students and researchers from underrepresented communities facing financial barriers"; "Priority will be given to authors, first-time attendees and individuals from underrepresented communities"; example justification: "I live in a developing country".

name: ICML Financial Aid
amount: In-person: registration + 7-night hotel; virtual: virtual registration (no travel support)
eligibility: Individuals for whom attending would be a financial burden; ICML account email must be linked to accepted paper(s)
eligibility_note: No nationality restriction on official page.
how_to_apply_tip: Incomplete answers lead to automatic rejection; link your OpenReview/ICML account to the accepted paper before applying.
deadline_quote: ICML 2026: applications closed on "18 May 2026 Aoe"; ICML 2027 page not yet published (404).
verdict_reason: Open to anyone for whom attending is a financial burden, with no country, age or career-stage restriction; requires an accepted ICML paper linked to the account.
eligibility_quote: Grants are "intended for individuals for whom attending the conference would cause a financial burden." "We are unable to provide travel support."

name: IEEE RAS Member Support - Developing Country Travel Support (ICRA, IROS, CASE)
amount: Typically valued at USD 1,500; for ICRA 2027 given as prepaid hotel rooms by RAS with limited exceptions
eligibility: RAS members from developing countries (IEEE Developing Country Listing) with an accepted paper; also student members
eligibility_note: Explicitly for 'RAS members from developing countries, as defined by IEEE's Developing Country Listing'; Pakistan is a lower-middle-income country.
how_to_apply_tip: Relevant for robot learning / embodied AI papers; join RAS (developing-country dues) before applying.
deadline_quote: ICRA 2027 travel support page: application deadline "(Schedule TBD)". ICRA 2026 deadline was 25 Feb 2026.
verdict_reason: Non-student RAS members from IEEE-listed developing countries with accepted papers qualify; Pakistan is on IEEE's List of Developing Nations; no age/career/institution limit. Requires RAS membership and an accepted ICRA paper.
eligibility_quote: "Members of IEEE Robotics and Automation Society with accepted papers, from developing countries as determined by the" IEEE Developing Country Listing; IEEE 'List of Developing Nations' includes "Pakistan".

name: IEEE SPS Conference Travel Grants (ICASSP / ICIP)
amount: Typically up to USD 750 (same region as conference) or up to USD 1,500 (other regions)
eligibility: Student and non-student authors with an accepted ICASSP/ICIP paper presented in person; active SPS membership; reference letter from supervisor/senior colleague
eligibility_note: Open to all countries; official page states applicants from developing countries receive higher priority.
how_to_apply_tip: Window is short (~10 days, e.g. 16-26 Jan 2026 for ICASSP 2026); join SPS (reduced developing-country fee) before applying and prepare the reference letter in advance for ICASSP 2027.
deadline_quote: Latest listed cycle: "Application Closed: 15 May 2026 at 23:59 (midnight) ET (Late Application will not be accepted)" (ICIP 2026). No ICASSP 2027 call posted yet.
verdict_reason: Grants are open to non-student authors in developing countries with priority for developing countries; no age, career-stage or institution restriction. Requires active SPS membership, accepted ICASSP/ICIP paper, in-person attendance and a reference letter.
eligibility_quote: Grants go to "student authors and non-student authors in developing and non-developing countries." "Higher priority will be given to eligible applicants from developing countries."

name: IJCAI Travel Grants (IJCAI Organization / AIJ)
funder: IJCAI Organization & Artificial Intelligence Journal Division
amount: See website (reimbursement; amount not published)
eligibility: Students, junior scientists and scientists attending IJCAI; priority to students and those with an accepted technical paper
eligibility_note: Official 2026 call lists no country restriction; applicants must state other sources of support and first seek departmental/local AI society funding.
how_to_apply_tip: Email the form with subject 'GRANT APPLICATION DOCUMENTATION'; include proof that HEC/institutional support was sought or insufficient.
deadline_quote: IJCAI-26: applications due "no later than June 4, 2026, midnight, AoE." No IJCAI-27 call found.
verdict_reason: Call covers "scientists" as well as students and junior scientists, with no country, age or institution restriction stated; priority goes to students and paper authors.
eligibility_quote: Grants are for "students, junior scientists and scientists" attending IJCAI-ECAI-26. Applicants "should first approach their department and/or local AI society for support before applying to IJCAI."

name: Machine Learning Summer School (MLSS) 2027 Okinawa
funder: Okinawa Institute of Science and Technology (OIST)
amount: No travel grant. Accommodation is provided in kind to a limited number of accepted participants (OIST housing or a shared hotel room). Registration fee for academics is about JPY 120,000.
eligibility: Mainly Master's/PhD students; small number of researchers, professors and practitioners also considered
eligibility_note: No nationality restriction stated; visa invitation letters provided. Postdoc admission not explicitly mentioned (falls under 'researchers').
how_to_apply_tip: Check the Application page immediately - the window may be closing; request a visa invitation letter from mlss2027@oist.jp right after acceptance.
deadline_quote: Poster abstract deadline (official application deadline): September 30, 2026 ... CV & references / OpenReview site closes: October 10, 2026
verdict_reason: The school is open to all applicants, and faculty can be admitted to a limited number of places. There are no nationality, age or institution limits. However, the 2027 application window closed on 2026-09-30, with OpenReview closing on 2026-10-10. No travel money is offered, only in-kind housing, and academics pay a fee of about JPY 120,000.
eligibility_quote: MLSS Okinawa 2027 is open to all applicants. ... Our main target audience is master's and Ph.D. students ... A small number of industry practitioners, professors, researchers ... may also be considered. | Accommodation support does not cover travel expenses.

name: NeurIPS Financial Assistance
amount: Complimentary in-person or virtual registration and prepaid accommodation up to 7 nights (Atlanta, Sydney or Paris); flights, meals and per diem not reimbursed
eligibility: Anyone for whom attending is a financial burden; priority to students and junior postdocs who are primary contributors to accepted NeurIPS work
eligibility_note: No country restriction on official page; location-specific travel burden is a selection factor.
how_to_apply_tip: Only one application per person and you must be logged in to neurips.cc; pair it with HEC airfare since NeurIPS does not cover flights.
deadline_quote: NeurIPS 2026: "6 Oct 23:59 AoE" (applications closed); NeurIPS 2027 call not published.
verdict_reason: Program supports participation across all NeurIPS tracks with no nationality, age or career-stage exclusion; students/junior postdocs only get priority.
eligibility_quote: The program "supports participation across all NeurIPS 2026 tracks and programs." "Priority may be given to students and junior postdoctoral researchers"; applications "evaluated holistically based on accessibility needs, financial hardship, first-time attendance, service to NeurIPS."

name: Simons Institute Research Fellowships (Fall 2027: Diffusion Generative Modeling)
funder: Simons Institute for the Theory of Computing, UC Berkeley
amount: Competitive salary and benefits; visa and housing assistance
eligibility: Early-career researchers within about 5 years of PhD in theoretical CS / ML theory
eligibility_note: No nationality restriction stated on the official pages.
how_to_apply_tip: Apply to the semester program closest to your research (cover letter, CV and research statement in one PDF, plus 3 referees).
deadline_quote: The application period opens on October 1, 2026, and applications are due December 1, 2026.
verdict_reason: Your PhD (after Nov 2024) is well within the 5-year post-PhD window, and faculty may apply. The page sets no nationality, age or institution rule. The fit with a theory-focused programme (Diffusion Generative Modeling) is a competitiveness issue, not an eligibility one.
eligibility_quote: Simons Institute Research Fellowships are intended for exceptional young scientists (within at most five years post-PhD the start of the 2027–28 academic year). ... Applicants who already hold junior faculty or postdoctoral positions are welcome to apply. ... Salaries and benefits are competitive, and assistance with visas and housing will be provided.

name: MSCA Staff Exchanges 2027 (HORIZON-MSCA-2027-SE-01-01)
amount: EUR unit costs per person-month of secondment (see call)
eligibility: Staff of consortium partner organisations (any career stage) actively engaged in the project
eligibility_note: Pakistan is on the Horizon Europe list of low/middle-income countries automatically eligible for funding, so Pakistani partner staff secondments can be funded.
how_to_apply_tip: You cannot apply alone: join an EU-led consortium as a Pakistani partner. Contact EU AI groups now, since the 2027 call is expected to open 15 Dec 2026.
deadline_quote: EU Funding & Tenders Portal topic HORIZON-MSCA-2027-SE-01-01: status Forthcoming; planned opening 2026-12-15; deadline 2027-04-15 (single stage). Previous call HORIZON-MSCA-2026-SE-01-01 closed 2026-04-16.
verdict_reason: Staff of any nationality and career stage can be seconded, and Pakistan is on the official list of low- and middle-income countries eligible for funding. The applicant must join a consortium with at least two organisations from EU or Associated Countries, and BIC must be a legal entity.
eligibility_quote: Staff can be researchers at any career stage ... can be of any nationality. | To be eligible for funding, applicants must be established in one of the following countries: ... the following low- and middle-income countries: ... Pakistan, Palau, Palestine ...

name: IPAM Long Program Participation – Artificial Intelligence in Materials Science (Fall 2027)
funder: Institute for Pure and Applied Mathematics (IPAM), UCLA (NSF)
amount: Financial support (housing and travel) for extended participation; amount not stated
eligibility: Researchers at all career stages; early-career participants encouraged
eligibility_note: No nationality restriction stated on the IPAM page.
how_to_apply_tip: Watch the program page and apply as soon as the form opens; stress your ML for scientific modeling work.
deadline_quote: Applications will be accepted through Friday, April 16, 2027, but offers may be made at any time, up to one year before the start date. Applications received after the deadline will still be considered if there is space available.
verdict_reason: Funding is open to researchers at all career levels in this area. The page has no nationality, age or institution restriction, and your AI/ML background fits the program theme.
eligibility_quote: We typically offer support to recent PhDs, graduate students, and researchers in the early stages of their career; however, mathematicians and scientists at all levels who are interested in this area are encouraged to apply for funding.

name: Training and Research in Italian Laboratories (TRIL)
amount: EUR 1,500 per month (PhD under 5 years old) or EUR 1,600 per month (PhD over 5 years old), plus a prepaid ticket and health insurance if needed. The host lab is expected to co-fund.
duration: A few months, up to a maximum of 24 months including extensions
eligibility: Nationals of and residents in a developing country with at least a Master's; physics-related fields incl. computational physics, wireless ICT/IoT, digital fabrication
eligibility_note: ICTP: applicants must be nationals of a developing country and live in one when selected; developed-country individuals are not eligible.
how_to_apply_tip: Find an Italian lab among ICTP's 400+ partner institutes first and get them to agree to co-fund; frame AI work within computational physics or ICT/IoT.
deadline_quote: Deadline 31 Dec 2027
verdict_reason: The applicant is a Pakistani national living in Pakistan (on ICTP's supported-country list) and holds more than a Master's. No age, gender or institution limits are stated.
